Olivia (Auditor): Hi team — quick auditor ask. We need cryptographic evidence that the KMS keywrap rotation on 2025-11-12 did not break provenance for objects written in that window. Specifically:
- mapping of old_key_id -> new_key_id (rotation record)
- S3 object metadata for affected buckets showing the KMS key id at write-time (versions if possible)
- RBAC change events (who changed what roles) correlated to the rotation window
Can you provide an export + short narrative (one paragraph) describing how these artifacts prove continuity? Need by end of week. Thanks :pray:

Anna (security): @Olivia ack. I'll gather the rotation record and role-change logs. tagging @Mike for S3 metadata extraction and @Lewis to double-check oncall logs for any alerts during rotation.

Mike (infra): I can pull S3 object versions and show the encryption metadata. Doing a quick query now. Example CLI we'll run:
```
aws s3api list-object-versions --bucket redwood-artifacts-prod --prefix models/ --query 'Versions[?LastModified>=`2025-11-12T00:00:00Z` && LastModified<=`2025-11-13T00:00:00Z`].{Key:Key,VersionId:VersionId,LastModified:LastModified,ETag:ETag}'
```
Then for metadata per version:
```
aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-artifacts-prod --key "models/foo.bin" --version-id <VERSIONID>
# look for ServerSideEncryption and SSEKMSKeyId
```
Will produce CSV with key, version, write-time, kmsKeyId.

Lewis (oncall): Oncall checked — no alerts tied to rotation window. I pulled CloudTrail events for kms:RotateKey and for IAM role changes. Quick Splunk query I used:
```
index=cloudtrail eventName=RotateKey OR eventName=UpdateRole OR eventName=PutRolePolicy earliest="2025-11-12T00:00:00" latest="2025-11-13T00:00:00"
| table _time userIdentity.accountId userIdentity.arn eventName requestParameters
```
I can attach the CSV export.

Anna (security): For the KMS keywrap mapping, we have the KMS rotation record exported from CloudTrail/AWS KMS. Example log snippet we'll include:
```
{ "eventTime": "2025-11-12T03:14:22Z", "eventName": "EnableKeyRotation", "userIdentity": {"arn":"arn:aws:iam::111122223333:user/ops"}, "requestParameters": {"keyId":"arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/old-key-id"}, "responseElements": {"status":"Success"}, "additionalEventData": {"newKeyId":"arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/new-key-id"} }
```
We'll include the full timestamps and the key ARNs.

Olivia (Auditor): That looks good. Two questions:
1) Can you confirm how S3 preserves the original KMS key id after a keywrap rotation? Auditor mindset: we need to see that objects encrypted before rotation still reference the old key id in metadata or a clear re-wrap record.
2) For RBAC changes, can you show both the pre- and post-change snapshots (role bindings) and the exact IAM principal that executed the rotation?

Anna (security): Short answers:
1) S3 object metadata stores the SSE-KMS key id used at encryption time. Rotation of the KMS CMK (i.e., creating a new key and re-wrapping) does not retroactively modify object metadata unless you explicitly re-encrypt objects. We will show head-object outputs proving original kmsKeyId on older versions + any rewrap activity logs if rewrap occurred.
2) We'll provide IAM role snapshots (exported via `aws iam get-role` and `aws iam list-attached-role-policies`) for timestamps immediately before and after the rotation, plus the CloudTrail principal that called the rotation API.

Mike (infra): Note — we found one object that was re-encrypted by a background job on 2025-11-12T05:40Z (job id bg-rewrap-42). We'll include that trace: job logs, start/end, and the object version ids affected. If auditors want, we can exclude rewrapped objects or annotate them.

deploy-bot: export-job-7911110000-xfer started by @Anna (security) — attaching temporary link when complete :white_check_mark:

Anna (security): I'll package the artifacts into a proof bundle with:
- cloudtrail_kms_rotation_20251112.csv
- s3_versions_kms_metadata_20251112.csv
- iam_role_snapshots_before_after_20251112.json
- narrative_proof_20251112.txt
Expect upload to shared drive & notify here within 3 hours.

Olivia (Auditor): Awesome — please include one-sentence statement for each artifact explaining what it proves (e.g., "cloudtrail_kms_rotation... shows old->new key mapping and principal ARN that performed rotation"). That will speed verification. :+1:

Lewis (oncall): uploaded cloudtrail extract to s3://redwood-compliance/evidence/2025-11-12/kms-rotation/cloudtrail_kms_rotation_20251112.csv
Mike (infra): uploaded s3 metadata CSV to same path. Anna (security): narrative uploaded and linked in the drive. deploy-bot: presigned link valid 7 days: https://redwood-files.example/7911110000/proof-bundle.zip

Olivia (Auditor): Received, thanks. I'll review and open any follow-ups. If everything aligns, we'll mark the control as satisfied for the rotation window. :white_check_mark:

Anna (security): Thanks everyone — ping me if you see follow-ups from auditor."
